sections.html:
Northern Davis County holds Syracuse, a city of about 10 square miles on the Great Salt Lake's east shore, roughly 30 miles from Salt Lake City and wedged between the lake and Interstate 15 at 4,272 feet. Neighbors are West Point to the north, Clearfield to the east and northeast and Layton to the southeast. A causeway off State Route 127 leads to Antelope Island, which is why the city bills itself as the island's gateway. Buyers enjoy that access, though wetlands on the west side restrict what can be built.

Few Utah cities have grown this quickly. Counts rose from 4,658 in 1990 to 9,398 in 2000, 24,331 in 2010 and 32,141 in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,909. Most houses were built during that surge and are newer than those in older suburbs along the Wasatch Front. For pricing, the ages of the roof, water heater and furnace count for more than the neighborhood's age.

Housing measureSyracuse
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate39,909
Owner-occupied housing rate89.7%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$573,300
Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage$2,073
Median monthly owner costs without a mortgage$571
Median gross rent$2,140
Households9,721
Persons per household3.64
Median household income$133,443

Housing and income rows cover 2020 to 2024. Read the median value as a survey estimate, since only an appraisal can value your own house.

State Route 177, the West Davis Corridor, opened January 6, 2024. Its northwest path through Syracuse has interchanges at 2000 West and Antelope Drive, and the opening segment stretches 16 miles from Farmington to West Point at a cost of $750 million.

Travel patterns on the county's west side shifted, and attention turned to nearby land. Syracuse is working on a 169-acre redevelopment zone called the WDC Gateway Community Reinvestment Area, at Antelope Drive and 3000 West, meant for housing, retail and commercial uses.

  • Most of that land is farmed or vacant and needs wetland mitigation, a hurdle the city calls significant.
  • UDOT is planning a 2.5-mile extension north to 1800 North in West Point, with work continuing through 2027.

New construction nearby appeals to some buyers and puts off others. A cash buyer simply values the house as it is today.

Summers run hot and winters are genuine. Highs commonly hit 95 degrees, and extremes have reached 106 degrees and minus 16 degrees. Average precipitation is about 24 inches and snowfall about 39 inches a year, with monsoon storms rolling in from late July to mid-September.

Roofs, gutters and grading take punishment from that mix, and freeze-thaw cycles and snow load shorten the life of decks, driveways and sprinkler lines.

  • Inspect the roof and flashing once winter ends and again after monsoon season.
  • Check the slope of the ground beside the foundation so snowmelt and rain drain away.
  • Blow out the sprinkler lines each fall ahead of a hard freeze.

The Davis School District serves the city, alongside the Syracuse Arts Academy charter campuses, which are public and enroll separately. Syracuse High School opened in 2007, and elementary schools include Cook, Syracuse Elementary, Bluff Ridge and Buffalo Point. Parents tend to ask about boundaries right away, so find the assigned school for your address before you advertise.

City code chapter 10.35 governs home businesses and temporary sales, which is useful if you are emptying a house. A garage or yard sale runs up to three consecutive days with no license, and four such events a year are allowed.

  • A minor home occupation is allowed in residential zones when it takes no more than 300 square feet or 20% of the floor area.
  • A home occupation permit cannot be transferred and ends when the holder leaves the address, so a buyer applies anew.
  • Unless state law exempts the business, a business license is needed.

Running a daycare, salon or similar business out of the house? Warn the buyer that the permit stays with you. For other questions, call Syracuse City planning.

Payment to Davis County is due November 30. Under Utah Code 59-2-1331, paying late costs a 2.5% penalty or $10, whichever is greater. When the date lands on a weekend or holiday, it shifts to the next business day. A primary residence is 45% exempt, up to one acre, and the title company divides the current bill at closing.

A Notice of Assessors' Property Market Valuation arrives at the end of July. The Davis County Commission sits as the Board of Equalization and takes appeals until September 15, so do not wait.

  • Only the market value can be appealed, never the tax rate.
  • Acceptable proof includes closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales or evidence of an error in the assessor's data.
  • Visit Tax Administration at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, or call 801-451-3331.

Pull together a few documents before you ask for an offer: your latest valuation notice or tax bill, the mortgage payoff figure if there is a loan, and the dates for the roof, water heater and furnace. If you hold a home occupation permit, a lease or a wetland or drainage record, bring that too.

After you accept, a title company checks the ownership record and prepares the settlement statement. You sign, the deed is recorded and your proceeds are paid. Nobody waits for a bank, so you can close as soon as the title work is clear or on a later date that suits your move.

If wetlands or drainage affect your lot, tell the buyer early. A house on the west side may carry limits on additions or outbuildings, and a buyer who learns that from you is less likely to renegotiate after a site visit. The same goes for any lake-effect dampness in a basement or crawl space, which is worth checking after a wet spring.

sections.h2: Who sells here and what a cash sale offers
sections.html:
Owners occupy 89.7% of Syracuse homes, with 3.64 people in the average household. People who contact us usually have a reason to move fast, whether a new job, a divorce, a family that outgrew the house or an inherited property nobody wants.

Listing suits a clean, updated house. If yours needs work, or you would rather skip showings and waiting, ask for a cash offer and compare. We buy as is, you set the closing date and you can say no. A title company runs the closing and pays any unpaid tax or mortgage from your proceeds.

faqs.q: How many people live in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: About 39,909 by the July 1, 2025 estimate, up from 32,141 in 2020, a gain of more than 7,000 people.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The survey figure for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024 is $573,300. It is not an appraisal of your house.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By November 30, or the next business day when that date is a weekend or holiday. A late payment adds 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Syracuse property valuation?
faqs.a: Yes. Notices arrive at the end of July and appeals close September 15. Only the market value can be appealed, using evidence like comparable sales or an appraisal.

faqs.q: Will you buy a Syracuse house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy as is, with no repairs or cleaning needed before an offer, and you can decline at no cost.
